shared_elements: large circular disc/rosette motif as a dominant central emblem
vertical slab surface organised into upper and lower zones
schematic incised linear figures set above the disc
framing or bordering lines along the slab edges
small schematic animal- or limb-like figures
justification: Both are upright slabs bearing a single large circular emblem (concentric ring in A, swirling multi-armed whirl in B) placed as the dominant motif in the middle of the field, with smaller schematic incised figures set in the zone above it and linear framing/banding elsewhere. The biggest difference in content is that A is an overtly anthropomorphic figure-stela with a modelled head, face and body ornaments plus chevron bands, while B shows only flat, purely graphic signs — a quadruped and a forked figure — with no human body being represented by the stone itself.
